title: Talking About Prices
subtitle: How to discuss costs, currency, and payment with confidence
description: Learn the words and phrases sales professionals use to talk about prices — 'It costs…', 'The rate is…', 'I can send you a quote' — so you can discuss money clearly and confidently with any customer.
dialogueSubtitle: Riley explains Brightline's pricing to Dana before she makes a decision

vocabulary.example: The Growth Plan costs $149 a month.

vocabulary.definition: Money you pay for a specific service, often a one-time charge.
vocabulary.example: There is no setup fee — you only pay the monthly rate.

vocabulary.definition: A fixed amount charged for something, usually per unit or time period.
vocabulary.example: If you pay annually, the monthly rate works out lower.

vocabulary.definition: Happening or paid once a year.
vocabulary.example: The annual plan saves you about $300 compared to paying monthly.

vocabulary.definition: A document that shows how much a customer owes for a service.
vocabulary.example: We send an invoice at the start of each billing period.

vocabulary.definition: A written estimate showing the price of a product or service.
vocabulary.example: I can send you a quote today with a full breakdown of costs.

vocabulary.definition: The type of money used in a particular country.
vocabulary.example: We bill in US dollars, but the invoice can show the amount in your currency.

vocabulary.definition: Money you do not have to spend; the difference between two prices.
vocabulary.example: Switching to annual billing gives you a saving of over $300 a year.

phrasalVerbs.definition: Give the price of something directly and simply.
phrasalVerbs.example: The Starter Plan costs $49 a month — it's our most affordable option.

phrasalVerbs.definition: State the price per unit or time period.
phrasalVerbs.example: If you pay annually, the monthly rate is $124 instead of $149.

phrasalVerbs.definition: Explain the effective price after a discount or different billing period.
phrasalVerbs.example: Annual billing works out at about $124 a month — a saving of $25.

phrasalVerbs.definition: Tell someone how you bill for a product or service.
phrasalVerbs.example: We charge monthly by default, but you can switch to annual any time.

phrasalVerbs.phrase: I CAN SEND YOU A QUOTE
phrasalVerbs.definition: Offer to provide a written price estimate for the customer.
phrasalVerbs.example: I can send you a quote today with a full breakdown in your currency.

phrasalVerbs.definition: Tell a customer that a cost or restriction does not exist.
phrasalVerbs.example: There is no setup fee and there is no contract — you can cancel any time.

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: Let me walk you through how our pricing works, Dana. The Starter Plan [[cost:to have a particular price]]s $49 a month.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: And what does the Growth Plan cost?

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: The Growth Plan is $149 a month. But if you pay [[annual:happening or paid once a year]]ly, the [[rate:a fixed amount charged for something, usually per unit or time period]] works out at about $124 a month.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: That's a decent [[saving:money you do not have to spend; the difference between two prices]]. Is there a setup [[fee:money you pay for a specific service, often a one-time charge]]?

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: No — there is no setup fee and no contract. The price you see is what you pay.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: How do you charge — monthly or annually?

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: We charge monthly by default, but you can switch to annual billing at any time. We send an [[invoice:a document that shows how much a customer owes for a service]] at the start of each month.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: Can I get a [[quote:a written estimate showing the price of a product or service]] in writing before we decide?

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: Of course. I can send you a quote today. Which [[currency:the type of money used in a particular country]] would you prefer — dollars or euros?

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: Euros would be easier for our accounts team.

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: No problem at all. I'll send a quote in euros within the hour.

chooseResponse.instructions: Work in groups. Read the customer's line, then discuss which response (A, B, or C) is best. Choose your answer together, then click to see if you were right — and why.

options: It depends on a lot of different factors.
The Growth Plan costs $149 a month. On annual billing, the rate works out at $124 — that's a saving of $25 a month.
I'll send you a quote and you can see the prices there.
items.explanation: B is correct. It gives the price clearly and immediately shows the annual saving — which shows value. A is vague and unhelpful. C delays the answer when you can give the price right now.

options: No — the price you see is all you pay. There are no hidden fees.
There might be a small fee depending on your plan.
Let me check what the current fee structure is and get back to you.
items.explanation: A is correct. It gives a clear, confident answer and adds the reassurance that there are no hidden costs — which customers care about. B creates doubt. C sounds unprepared for a very basic question.

items.customerLine: Can we pay monthly instead of annually?
options: Annual billing is better — you save more money that way.
Monthly billing costs more, so most customers choose annual.
Of course — we charge monthly by default, so that is no problem at all.
items.explanation: C is correct. It confirms what the customer wants clearly and without pushback. A ignores the customer's preference and pushes for something else. B leads with a negative and may feel like pressure.

items.customerLine: Can I get the price in euros instead of dollars?
options: We only bill in US dollars, I'm afraid.
I'll have to check with our finance team and get back to you.
Of course — I can send you a quote in euros. It's easy to adjust the currency on the invoice.
items.explanation: C is correct. It says yes immediately and explains how — which is exactly what the customer wants to hear. A says no when it is not necessary. B creates an unnecessary delay for a simple request.

profileMatch.instructions: Read each customer's situation. As a group, decide which billing arrangement fits them best — monthly, annual, or per-seat. Use phrases from this lesson like 'The rate is…' and 'It works out at…' to explain your thinking. Click 'Check Matches' when you agree.

profiles.name: Felix
profiles.description: Felix runs a small studio with fluctuating project volume. Some months he needs 5 seats, other months just 2. He wants to keep costs flexible and doesn't want to pay for seats he isn't using.

profiles.name: Mia
profiles.description: Mia's team size is stable and she's confident they'll use the tool all year. Her manager asked her to reduce the monthly invoice amount. She's happy to commit to a full year if it means a lower rate.

profiles.name: Alex
profiles.description: Alex is testing Brightline before recommending it to his board. He doesn't want to sign a contract or commit to an annual fee until he is sure it works for his organisation. Budget approval will take time.

options.label: Monthly billing — no contract
options.description: Pay month by month with no commitment. The rate is $149 a month for up to 25 users. There is no annual contract and you can cancel any time. Best for teams that are still evaluating.

options.label: Annual billing — discounted rate
options.description: Pay for the full year upfront. It works out at $124 a month — a saving of $25 compared to monthly billing. Best for teams that are committed and want to reduce their monthly cost.

options.label: Per-seat billing — flexible
options.description: Pay only for active users each month. The rate is $19 per seat. Best for teams with variable headcount or seasonal projects where the number of active users changes month to month.

finishTheLine.instructions: The salesperson's line has been cut off. As a group, discuss how you would finish it. Try to use 'It costs…', 'The rate is…', or 'It works out at…'. There is no single correct answer — compare your ideas, then click to see one possible answer.

items.customerLine: That seems like a lot to pay every month.
items.salespersonStart: I understand. If you switch to annual billing, it works out at
items.suggestedCompletion: about $124 a month — that is a saving of over $300 a year. A lot of customers find that makes the decision much easier.

items.customerLine: What exactly do I get for that price?
items.suggestedCompletion: deal tracking, customer management, and reporting for up to 25 users. That also includes 24/7 support and a free 14-day trial to start.

items.customerLine: We need to get internal approval before we commit to any cost.
items.salespersonStart: That is completely fine. I can send you a formal quote today so you have
items.suggestedCompletion: everything you need for the approval process — the price, what is included, the payment options, and the currency you prefer.

items.customerLine: Is the price the same for all team sizes?
items.salespersonStart: The rate is the same regardless of how many users you have, as long as
items.suggestedCompletion: you are within the plan limit. The Growth Plan covers up to 25 users, so it actually works out cheaper per person as your team grows.
